articles.title: Alchemy - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Alchemy is the process of converting substances into other materials. In The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, alchemy is utilized to craft Potions, Oils, Bombs and
articles.body:
Alchemy is the process of converting substances into other materials. In The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , alchemy is utilized to craft Potions, Oils, Bombs and Decoctions that can be used to enhance Geralt as you play. This guide covers how to craft items using alchemy, where to obtain the different recipes and their requirements, and what the various concoctions do.

Use the links below to skip to key sections of this guide:

A number of alchemy recipes can be found and crafted, encompassing four main categories:

Looted at random or bought from a merchant, there are only a few recipes you can obtain at specific times or locations in the game.

Bombs that can be crafted are large in effect. They can be tossed either by manually aiming by holding down the appropriate button, or tossed automatically when locked on to a target.

Decoctions are special and potent elixirs that use a monster's mutagens to give Geralt some of their powers, if only for a time. These decoctions are often hard to brew, and require you to kill the monster you wish to borrow powers from. Their effects vary wildly, and usually have high toxicity.

You can coat your blades in oils that can further damage a monster - if the recipe for the appropriate oil is known. Oils effect categories of enemies, not just one specific creature. Once made, an oil can be applied any time, and will last for several hits. During this time, all strikes against the target will deal additional damage.

Beast Oil : Bears, Boars, Guard dogs, Wild dogs, Wolves, Wargs, White Wolves

Cursed Oil : Berserkers, Botchlings, Ulfhedinn, Werewolves

Draconid Oil : Basilisks, Cockatrices, Forktails, Wyverns

Elementa Oil : Djinns, Earth Elementals, Fire Elementals, Gargoyles, Golems, Hounds of the Wild Hunt, Ice Elementals

Hanged Man's Venom : Bandits, Deserters, Renegades, Renegade leaders, Skelligers, Pirates

Hybrid Oil : Archgriffins, Ekhidna, Erynias, Griffins, Harpies, Sirens, Succubi

Insectoid Oil : Arachas (both Armored and Venomous), Arachasae, Arachnomorph, Endrega drones, Endrega warriors, Endrega workers

Necrophage Oil : Alghouls, Bilge hags, Devourers, Drowners, Drowned dead, Foglets, Ghouls, Grave hags, Mucknixers, Rotfiends, Water hags

Ogroid Oil : Cyclopses, Ice Giant, Ice trolls, Nekkers, Nekker Warriors, Rock trolls

Relict Oil : Ancient Leshans, Chorts, Crones, Dopplers, Fiends, Godlings, Leshans

Specter Oil : Nightwraiths, Noonwraiths, Plague Maidens, Wraiths

Vampire Oil : Ekimmaras, Higher Vampires, Katakans

A Witcher can make use of powerful potions that would be lethal to a normal human. These specialty potions can do everything from granting night vision, increased regenerative capabilities, and more. Once a potion is crafted, it can be replenished at any time by meditating with enough pure alcohol in your inventory.

Even though there are different categories of Alchemy items you can create, they are all made using the same process.

Obtain the recipe for the item you want to make. You start the game with a few already known.

As long as you have all the ingredients needed, confirm to make the item

You can do this at any time and no special tools are required. You're also able to craft items when shopping from an herbalist .

Once you've made the recipe you'll see it disappear from the available crafting list. Instead, all you need to do is meditate with a strong alcohol, such as Alcohest, in your inventory for them to be refilled.

While alchemy is great to boost your combat ability and keep you healthy, there are some downsides to chugging witcher concoctions. Each potion or decoction you create has a certain level of toxicity to it. If you drink too many at once, you will become sick and begin to lose health. Toxicity can be cured by meditating or taking White Honey.

Alchemy substances and ingredients are items found throughout the world and required when making any alchemical recipe. Some you can craft yourself, while others you can buy or collect while exploring.

Mutagens are obtained from monsters after they're slain and are necessary when making decoctions.

articles.title: Scavenger Hunt: Cat School Gear - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Feline Witcher Gear Set can be found in Novigrad, as part of the Side Quest Scavenger Hunt: Cat School Gear. It consists of 7 pieces -- 5 armor pieces, 2
articles.body:
The Feline Witcher Gear Set can be found in Novigrad, as part of the Side Quest Scavenger Hunt: Cat School Gear. It consists of 7 pieces -- 5 armor pieces, 2 swords, and 1 crossbow -- meaning you can fully kit out Geralt if you take the time to track down the diagrams.

Simply collect any of the pieces to start the treasure hunt; you don't need to accept a quest anywhere, just go to any of the locations and pick up the diagram. It's a lengthy process, but well worth your time, as the gear is powerful.

The recommended character level to wear the armor found in this hunt is 14, to get the most use out of its stats and special features.

At the ruins of Est Tayiar in the eastern part of Velen , descend through the large hole in the ground to the tunnel beneath. On your right is a wall that can be destroyed with Aard - behind it you will find a skeleton with the diagram.

Enter Drahim Castle, south of Novigrad, and descend the ladder to the lower floor. There you will find a chest containing the Steel Sword diagram.

Off the western coast of Redania (south-west of Novigrad) is a floating shipwreck near an island south of the lighthouse signpost. Climb aboard the ship and descend into the hold to find the chest containing the diagram.

Facing the tall tower on Novigrad's Temple Isle from the south, head down the switchback road and along the western cliffside behind the houses to find a path leading down below the tower.

You'll come across an Illusion, which you'll need Keira Metz's amulet (acquired during the main quest Wandering in the Dark ) to pass. Inside the main chamber is a Golem - defeat it and follow the steps up the path on the left-hand side of the cavern.

Climb up to the next chamber to find several statues surrounding a large area. Kill any Wraiths that may appear and rotate all of the statues so that they face inwards. Once the floor opens, eliminate the drowners and swim to the bottom of the cave to collect the Laboratory Key from the skeleton and return to the main chamber.

Once inside the laboratory, you'll find the now-crazed former Witcher known as Mad Kiyan. Defeat him and loot his corpse to find the armor diagrams for the Cat School.

articles.body:
Mutagens are dropped by the various monsters you can slay in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. There are a handful of general mutagens you can collect or craft with Alchemy, but species specific mutagens are more powerful. Here are all the specific mutagens, how to find them, and what they are used for.

These are the known guaranteed mutagen locations for each creature that has one. The monster it comes from may spawn in multiple areas, but facing a Wraith randomly doesn't ensure that a mutagen will drop. Typically, completing Witcher contracts will result in slaying the monster and obtaining the item.

General mutagens can drop as random loot when killing monsters. These are combined to create more advanced versions.

articles.title: Deadlock Tier List: Best Heroes - Deadlock Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Although Deadlock is still in development, and heroes are being rebalanced and modified, there's already plenty of conversation around the current
articles.body:
Although Deadlock is still in development, and heroes are being rebalanced and modified, there's already plenty of conversation around the current Deadlock tier list and which heroes may feel under- or over-tuned.

Use the below Deadlock Tier List tool to put together your own tier list and see the community tier list, which is the average of all user-submitted tier lists!

Below is the IGN Deadlock tier list, with explanations for each placement to follow.

S-tier characters are the best of the best right now; they are basically never a bad pick, are flexible with builds, and are incredibly difficult to deal with if they get ahead.

Baba is a true staple of the meta right now, arguably being the strongest character in the whole game. Because of her natural anti-spirit properties, she is a straightforward counter to the currently prevalent spirit-based meta, making her a strong counterpick.

On top of this, she also has a very strong kit outside of her Threadsap. Granny Long Legs is a great frontlining mobility tool, and Feed the Birds is a very powerful ultimate that can be frustrating to deal with, making Baba a serious threat no matter what.

Wraith has been arguably the best hypercarry in the game for a little while now, scaling absurdly well into the late game, and not having a weak enough midgame to offset this, meaning she can usually weather the storm of the early game well enough to get to where she can 1v11.

While her laning phase isn't the best, it can be deceptively good if you play around her damage spikes, such as her Tier 2 Card Trick and her ultimate. With her ult up and a full deck of cards, Wraith can be one of the scariest people to face in Deadlock, even without many core items. Additionally, the laning phase is not really important right now, making Wraith's one weakness rather irrelevant.

Abrams is the definitive 'tank' in Deadlock, and has been for a little while now. Arguably the most consistent character in the game, you can almost never go wrong with Abrams.

As the early game in Deadlock has grown less and less important, Abrams can survive his very weak laning phase to scale into the mid-to-late game, where he feels near unkillable while also being a serious damage threat, especially if you miss a parry.

Kelvin has soared up in winrate across all ranks in the game after the buffs to his Frozen Shelter with the Halloween patch, letting him fill the role of a scaling support/tank hybrid.

Kelvin is also another beneficiary of the laning phase being less important these days, as his laning is rather poor compared to most supports in the game.

Shiv got a few adjustments in the most recent major patch, but they only made him even better. His alt-fire is still remarkably powerful when building for gun damage, and his Serrated Knives got a damage increase as well, making him a strong frontline brawler.

On top of this, Shiv scales excellently, and thanks to the game currently placing more importance on the late game rather than the early game, you can bypass Shiv's woeful laning phase to reach your true power spikes.

Arguably the most flexible and versatile character in the game, Ivy can be played in a number of ways. Traditionally a support, Ivy has several tools to enable her allies, with her Air Drop and Kudzu Connection being particularly valuable.

However, even though she may be support-focused, she can absolutely fill a carry role on the team, either being a teamfight spirit threat or a pure gun damage carry, making her good no matter the situation or team comp.

Perhaps slightly overhated given she can be countered quite comfortably, Haze is still undeniably strong. She generally plays play as an assassin who looks for picks before the fight begins on high priority targets, or isolating individuals in 1v1s away from their team.

However, while the assassin playstyle may be her bread and butter, when ahead, she can simply mow down the entire enemy frontline, or at the very least force them to build items like Metal Skin and Plated Armor.

Celeste is a real nuisance at the moment to deal with. While she may not boast the most impressive winrate right now, this is not reflective of her true strength at all as she is simply a rather hard character to play.

Celeste is able to hold her own on the frontline, sustain from her high healing from Light Eater, as well as take 1v1 fights fairly consistently against a wide variety of characters.

While laning may not be as important right now, Paige's strength in the laning phase cannot be ignored. She is arguably the strongest laner in the entire game thanks to her Plot Armor shield and base weapon damage, letting her comfortably support weaker laners to help them scale into the late game.

On top of this, Paige doesn't have the worst scaling herself; while she may not be a serious threat later in the game, her ultimate is still teamfight-winning, and her midgame is strong enough that she can duel 1v1 if she is ahead.

Lady Geist has slowly crept back into relevance over the past few patches, and with her recent small buff to her spirit scaling on Essence Bomb, she is even stronger and more versatile than before.

While the bomb build on Geist may not be the best way to play her, it is still a viable option if you are more comfortable that way. She can be a bulky damage dealer; while not a pure tank, she is still definitely hard to kill.

A-tier heroes in Deadlock are generally good, but they are either a bit more situational or are slightly outclassed by alternatives in S-tier.

Graves has seen a bit of a surge in power ever since the "Tank Graves" build was discovered, boosting her from relative mediocrity to a standout pick.

Graves can be quite frustrating to play at times, particularly with this build as she can hold her ground in the frontline against some of the brawly characters in the meta right now.

Seven has crept up in power slowly but surely, and has cemented himself as a strong lategame hypercarry. However, he is kept out of S-tier as he is simply more situational and less survivable than certain alternatives like Wraith.

Seven can shine, though, in large team fights with his Storm Cloud. Once you get Unstoppable specifically, Seven is a serious presence that will command a lot of space.

Up Next: All Deadlock Characters: Hero Abilities, Scaling, and Stats

articles.title: Internal Mass Effect 2 Trailer Gives Us the Earliest Look at the Game Yet
articles.summary: The lead animator for Mass Effect 2 has shared a previously unreleased trailer for the game, only ever seen by the developers at BioWare.
articles.body:
The lead animator for Mass Effect 2 has shared a previously unreleased trailer for the game, only ever seen by the developers at BioWare.

This trailer, described as a demo reel of the in-progress cinematics, dates back to April 2009. It would have been used to demonstrate the kind of work that the animation team was doing for Mass Effect 2, and eagle-eyed fans will notice several scenes that did make it into the final game.

Fuck it - here's something for #N7Day I haven't shown before. A very pre-alpha internal trailer intended to highlight the cinematics we were creating in Montreal. Faces were the average of all the customisation sliders in Maya, and we ran every scene with each possible squamate when polishing. — Jonathan Cooper (@GameAnim) November 7, 2026

Fuck it - here's something for #N7Day I haven't shown before. A very pre-alpha internal trailer intended to highlight the cinematics we were creating in Montreal. Faces were the average of all the customisation sliders in Maya, and we ran every scene with each possible squamate when polishing.

Released by Jonathan Cooper, a game developer who has worked with the likes of BioWare, Ubisoft, and Naughty Dog, this Mass Effect 2 trailer gives us an incredibly early look at some of the game’s characters and pivotal moments. While it can be a little hard to make out, we can spot companions like Miranda, Garrus, and Jack.

Cooper hasn’t shared too much info on the trailer, but did say what it was like to work on it. “[…] remembering all the arguments and drama on the team haha,” he said. “But mostly reading the scripts and getting pumped imagining how awesome we could make Shepard look hitting those story beats.”

Mass Effect 2 was quite the departure from the first game, and this internal trailer makes that perfectly clear. After opening with Shepard’s death, we’re treated to a very ‘00s action movie monologue from the Commander themself, before cutting to the new Normandy crew.

If you’re curious about the song in the background, it’s C'Mon Try A Little Bit by Melodrone. It doesn’t appear to have been used in any of the promotional material that was shared with fans back in the day, and it only has 64,000 plays on YouTube.

All in all, this is nothing like the trailer we would be shown, cinematic or otherwise, but it does capture that edgier, action vibe that the sequel was going for, compared to its more optimistic predecessor. It’s a vibe that continues to resonate with fans to this day, as Mass Effect 2 is often held up as the best game BioWare ever put out.

Now, those same fans are fighting to protect the series they love. After EA closed BioWare and canceled Mass Effect 5 , the community started the Save Mass Effect campaign , which urges the publisher to do something with the series , whether that’s fund new games or licence it out to another developer. Some are also pushing for Mass Effect to be returned to those who worked on it.

Rhiannon (she/her) is a freelance journalist who has been in the industry since 2019. She won MCV's Women in Games award in 2025 and adores RPGs. You can follow her on Bluesky at @rhithewitch.

articles.title: Exterminauts Turns You and 2 Friends Into Intergalactic Pest Control Techs With Some Really Spicy Secondary Weapons | IGN Preview
articles.summary: I've played about five hours of the blue-collar bug-squasher so far, and admittedly it’s grown on me. The special launcher weapons and diverse array of weird-ass bugs keeps skirmishes interesting, and I'm still in the process of finding new jobs to do and new biomes to do them on, so the sense of discovery is still there. But I don't think Exterminauts has made an airtight case for horde shooter fans to choose it over their current favorite. It doesn't have the open-endedness of a Deep Rock Galactic, the slam-dunk tone and mood of Darktide, or the strong satirical comedy of Helldivers II. None of that is a death sentence, especially not this early in development. But it has its dirty work cut out for it.
articles.body:
Exterminauts feels a bit generic at first.

Its default weapons aren’t very new or exciting, but the secondary weapons are far more interesting.

Horde shooters are really the perfect games to double as a hang with your friends, as the objectives are typically pretty simple and clear, letting you chat hot goss over comms while you’re ripping hot lead in game. Because of this (and the key successes of a handful of them) these games are kind of everywhere in 2026, and after some hands on time with Exterminauts, a third-person co-op shooter that puts mad science tools in your hands in order to defend and upkeep the assets of your capitalist overlords, I think that fact is going to be their biggest issue. It's got a good look and rounds can produce some fun chaos, but I had a hard time not comparing this to all the games it’s clearly taking notes from and I was left questioning if it had the juice to get me to clock in for a long shift.

The gimmick and tone that ties it all together is fun at first, as you and your party work for the MegaCorp that needs its assets maintained and protected from the (implied) native bug threat that continues to rip and tear its infrastructure to pieces. This sort of “evil corporate master vs. exploited labor dynamic” is a fun starting point for a satirical world that never really gets bolted down. The banter between your dispatcher and the Planetary Director from the corporation is certainly quippy, but I didn’t find it very funny. There is a slapstick aura around everything you do, but many of the little barks and hollers characters do in the field sound like poor Deadpool impressions.

It’s pretty easy to list what Exterminauts does that happens to be a version of something you'll find somewhere else. So what does it do that’s unique? The tasks that bring you and your group of up to three to the planet surfaces often require input in ways that can be surprising. Helldivers II required a lot of d-pad inputs in order to fix computer glitches or call in support. Here, when you arrive on scene to fix some infrastructure damaged by the local wildlife, it often involves a bit more engaging resolutions. One that came up a few times was welding, where I have to follow the crack on the side of a pump with a flaming torch. It's not too complicated a pattern, just askew enough that you need to make some adjustments, but not so jagged as to be confusing or distracting while under enemy assault.

Another required two of us to work in tandem to ratchet some mechanical device up from bottom to top, with one side being able to only go so far before the other had to put their weight on it. “Required” is an exaggeration, in fairness, because you can definitely do this solo, but I liked these for how they encouraged people to work together to solve a problem, as opposed to just pushing buttons the right way. I didn't see too many other examples of these co-op chores in the limited maps and time we had with the demo, but I hope there are many more of these as development continues.

In addition, there are side jobs that pop up on your map when you’re nearby, which are supposed to be smaller sub-jobs for more minor rewards, like releasing a special elite monster to kill for some this-run-only reward. But I kept stumbling on to an abandoned mech, which was neither small nor minor. The punch it packs makes it super worth going to find it, but only one person at a time can pilot one, and when its ammo is gone it's gone. But this is a good measure of the dichotomy of these finds. I was pretty unmoved by the former and found the latter to be great every time.

Running from job to job when deployed means you’re destined to encounter some of the insidious insectoid fauna that exist to impede you. The concept of shooting your way through bugs to get from objective to objective is about as synonymous with the sci-fi extraction shooter as spouts are to tea kettles, but these beasties came in various forms and with novel quirks for each. There's some that are 80% mouth and leap long distances to put you in it. There’s some that have long necks that fan like the spitter dinosaur in Jurassic Park that kills Newman from Seinfeld, except they shoot lasers out of their big singular eye instead of poison. There’s floating Thanksgiving Day Parade balloon-looking ones that spit out flying jerks that shock you bioelectrically. These bugs are a wonderfully strange bunch to look at.

They can be tough to wrangle when they start to amass into a wave of teeth and legs, but the squads I was in didn't have much trouble. We didn't turn the difficulty up that high either - we spent our missions between 2 and 4 of a possible 8 levels as we learned the ropes and gained some basic gear. Things do get way more dangerous solo, where I was throwing lives directly into the shedder that was the alien menace. Upping the difficulty adds more and tougher pests, more potential repair jobs, and higher possibilities of environmental hazards like extreme weather and the like. Every extraction requires hunkering down and holding off a grand finale of waves while your ride comes to get you, and these were usually the most dangerous parts of the mission - though they were also the most perfect time to use your more rare support items, like sentry turrets and a tube you can attach yourself to to give yourself infinite ammo for a brief period of time.

Some of the tools you can employ to exterminate these pests are notable, but I found most of the assortment available to me at the time to be wanting. A smattering of kinetic bullet blasters sat comfortably in the well-known territory of “guns like the ones you’re already familiar with.” These assault rifles and SMGs were fine, operating well within the range of my expectations, though not being particularly impressive versions of what you’ve seen a hundred times. I don’t expect Call of Duty levels of detail, but some more compelling gun sounds and haptics would step these up dramatically.

Fortunately, the secondary weapons were a bit spicier. You default to a plasma sludge launcher, which sticks globs of caustic goo onto victims, piling on the corrosive debuff and doing damage over time. This fountain of pain is strong, and especially good for groups of enemies. On the flip side, I also got my hands on the CrossCut, a weapon that slings circular saw blades of a comically large size. When these hit enemies they stick to them, spinning in place and chewing through whatever is trapped there with it. You can charge these blades to extend the time this berserk beyblade delightfully does its dirty deed. All of these special weapons can be further buffed by pulling out a jumper cable sort of contraption to make the next shot a doozy at the expense of some battery power. This is an interesting mechanic that probably hides more value than I could shake out in only a couple of hours - maybe an enhanced weapon it can boost penetration values of or cause special side effects outside of just doing way more stagger and health damage. Each of these secondaries add a bunch of utility and dynamism to combat in a way that makes me wonder why the basic weapons are here at all.

You unlock access to these weapons through Sponsorships, which act almost like classes, giving you access to a unique passive ability that hypothetically sets the tone for how you play. The Bullet Crown sponsorship ups the damage you do on critical hits and provides access to a rapid-fire SMG, so aggressive damage-dealing is your forte. Conversely, Vardhan is focused on support, spreading some of the healing you get from your recovery items with other members of your squad. I don’t think I spent enough time playing to see these actually make squad members play differently, but I can see how having a mix of these passives in a group could be a benefit. I wouldn’t say that a Bullet Crown guy should focus more on shooting bugs than clearing objectives, or that a Vardhan should be hovering over life gauges like a WoW Cleric, but the boons they provide are obvious.

There are a lot of meta games to play as well. All of your gear can be upgraded so long as you have enough coins and other materials that can be found out in the field. Like Exterminauts’ contemporaries, there is a season pass filled with functional and cosmetic gear that you can earn the points for through play or just spend real money to unlock instantly. After gaining some levels, you’ll be able to add trinkets that give you even more passive buffs that I'm sure can be mixed and matched to get something resembling a focused and efficient build. There’s plenty of things to earn, and I seem to be getting the resources needed to buy and upgrade my gear at a pretty breezy pace, but it's hard to know how good any of this is without more time spent. There's also the biggest question: how much time am I really willing to spend to earn it?

I've played about five hours of the blue-collar bug-squasher so far, and admittedly it’s grown on me. The special launcher weapons and diverse array of weird-ass bugs keeps skirmishes interesting, and I'm still in the process of finding new jobs to do and new biomes to do them on, so the sense of discovery is still there. But I don't think Exterminauts has made an airtight case for horde shooter fans to choose it over their current favorite. It doesn't have the open-endedness of a Deep Rock Galactic, the slam-dunk tone and mood of Darktide, or the strong satirical comedy of Helldivers II. None of that is a death sentence, especially not this early in development. But it has its dirty work cut out for it.

While you're here, check out these recent previews of other big upcoming games we've checked out recently!

Jarrett Green is a frequent contributor to IGN. Talk video games with him on X/Twitter at @Jarrettjawn .

articles.title: Ekhidnas - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Ekhidnas are the more advanced form of the Siren in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. They are just as deadly in the water as they are in the air. Their attacks can
articles.body:
Ekhidnas are the more advanced form of the Siren in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt . They are just as deadly in the water as they are in the air. Their attacks can leave you momentarily disoriented and they often fight in packs. One wrong move could be fatal when you take on these monsters.

Found throughout Skellige, they inhabit shipwrecks, remote islands, and the mountaintops. When hunting ekhidnas for their drops, you'll want to stay away from water locations. While you can kill the creatures underwater or in the air with your crossbow, you won't be able to loot the corpses. Stick to the mountains or areas along the coast of Ard Skellig.

Ekhidna are found along Skellige's coast, specifically north of Arinbjorn towards Eldberg isle. They can spawn from Siren nests when destroyed, including the wrecked ship monster nest to the north of where you crash on Ard Skellig. One is located at the Guarded Treasure southeast of Kaer Muire and at the Elverum Lighthouse in the southwest of Ard Skellig. You'll find a group of them on the western coast of Faroe Island in Skellige. In the mountains, head to the Trail of Yngvar's Fang where they are located near the start of the trial. Melusine herself is encountered during the side quest Contract: Here Comes the Groom .

Like other flying creatures, landing a crossbow shot or hitting it with Aard will bring the target crashing to the ground where it is weakened. You can also burn it with Igni right when it swoops towards you, causing the monster to fumble to land as well as inflicting damage over time. If they land farther away, use a Grapeshot bomb for ranged damage as you close the distance. Then deal the fatal blows with your silver sword coated in Hybrid Oil .

Ekhidnas have a chance to drop a blue mutagen that's used as an ingredient in the Ekhidna Decoction . When equipped in a skill tree it enhances Sign intensity by 5%, scaling up to 20%.

articles.title: 8BitDo’s Ultimate 3C Plus controller gains Xbox compatibility and a cord.
articles.summary:
Less than a month after introducing its Ultimate 3C Plus controller with wireless PC and Android support, 8BitDo announced a wired version that’s Xbox compatible. At $39.99, it will be the same price as the wireless version when it launches on November 16th and features a pair of TMR thumbsticks with adjustable tension, switchable Hall effect triggers, an extra pair of shoulder buttons, and Windows support.

articles.body:
Last month, Cyberpunk 2077 got an ambitious multiplayer mod, NightCoop. This is great if you want to play with up to eight players, going through the main story with friends. However, if you want something even more chaotic, we now have another multiplayer project: Open//77. This essentially turns Cyberpunk 2077 into GTA Online, letting servers of often more than 100 players mess around in Night City, getting up to various roleplay shenanigans.

Open//77 was just released in alpha, meaning that anyone can now download it and give it a try themselves. You need to own both Cyberpunk 2077 and the Phantom Liberty expansion for it to work, but as long as that’s covered, you’re able to experience this new take on Night City.

While NightCoop is great if you want a pretty vanilla game experience, albeit with multiple Vs running around, Open//77 is more like a big playground. You have different roles and different tasks to get up to than in the base game. As you can also see in the footage, you can play in third-person.

Night City opens on November 6. Light RP, the official Open77 @CyberpunkGame multiplayer server. Make your crew, race, run contracts, hit the casino, rob Arasaka, fight a world boss, outrun the NCPD. Friday, 22:00 UTC — Open//77 (@open2077) November 4, 2026

Night City opens on November 6. Light RP, the official Open77 @CyberpunkGame multiplayer server. Make your crew, race, run contracts, hit the casino, rob Arasaka, fight a world boss, outrun the NCPD. Friday, 22:00 UTC

It also looks like there’s more of a focus on just hanging out in the open world. One video shows players meeting up in a room they rented to play a board game. There are also more aesthetic features to play around with, such as an expanded vehicle customisation menu.

level -1 of the card shop: private rooms. neon deck, cozy lounge, tatami room. open one, send the code to a friend to play together — Open//77 (@open2077) November 5, 2026

level -1 of the card shop: private rooms. neon deck, cozy lounge, tatami room. open one, send the code to a friend to play together

Vehicle customization is landing on Open77 @CyberpunkGame multiplayer. Any server can use it. RP, racing, car meets, whatever you're building. Open alpha and our Light RP server go live tonight, 22:00 UTC. — Open//77 (@open2077) November 6, 2026

Vehicle customization is landing on Open77 @CyberpunkGame multiplayer. Any server can use it. RP, racing, car meets, whatever you're building. Open alpha and our Light RP server go live tonight, 22:00 UTC.

Every server has its own theme. The most popular is NCRP, which supports up to 1,000 players looking to roleplay. Others are more combat, PvP focussed. Something to consider if you are interested is that Open//77 openly admits to using AI in the development process. Indeed, AI is why we are seeing so many fan-made projects like this released at once. It has divided the modding community , as many were making unofficial multiplayer mods like this long before generative AI was a factor. Earlier this month, Nexus Mods, the biggest platform for mods on the internet, reacted by enforcing mandatory disclosure for mods with AI-assisted code, and letting users filter AI-assisted mods out of their search criteria or preferences.

I tried Open//77 out, but it did not play nice with my heavily modded setup. Open//77 does support mods (and you can even temporarily download a host’s mods if you join their server), but messing around with my own mods so soon after having to fix them for the latest official update seemed a bit too daunting just now.

Wherever you land on projects like this, it’s no wonder there is an appetite for them. Cyberpunk 2077 was supposed to get an official multiplayer mode, but this was scrapped after the base game’s messy launch . A sequel is in development now, so we’ll have to wait and see if CD Projekt Red can make it work for that.

Rhiannon (she/her) is a freelance journalist who has been in the industry since 2019. She won MCV's Women in Games award in 2025 and adores RPGs. You can follow her on Bluesky at @rhithewitch.

articles.title: Sony Launches New PS Portal Model in Japan With Internal Storage for 'Future Functionality,' Changes Official Name
articles.summary: Sony is releasing a new model of the PlayStation Portal in Japan next month. The big difference is that it has internal storage, hinting that Sony might be expanding the handheld’s functions in the future.
articles.body:
Sony is releasing a new model of the PlayStation Portal in Japan next month. The big difference is that it has internal storage, hinting that Sony might be expanding the handheld’s functions in the future.

“With an eye towards future functionality, the new model comes with the brand new addition of internal storage,” teased Sony Japan’s official blog post . “We will provide further details regarding these future features as they are finalized.”

First released back in 2023 and looking like the stretch limo version of a PlayStation controller with an HD screen in the middle, the PlayStation Portal was originally designed as a way to play your PS5 games on handheld. Although this remote play function frees up your TV, it requires you to stream your games from your PS5 over Wi-fi.

The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time

In the official Playstation blog post announcing the new model, Sony emphasized that the Portal now allows “even players who don’t have a PS5” to enjoy PS5 games. Last year, Sony began giving PS Plus Premium members the option to stream games from the cloud to their PS Portal instead. With this new model release, Sony has also changed the full Japanese name of the handheld from “Playstation Portal Remote Player,” to simply “PlayStation Portal Player.” This suggests that the company is moving away from the Portal’s image as an accessory that streams from a PS5 console via Remote Play, to a more fully-fledged handheld.

It’s also possible that any new functions added to the PS Portal could be a testing ground for the upcoming PS6, which has long been rumored to involve a handheld. Back in June, Sony Interactive Entertainment CEO Hideaki Nishino commented that developing new console experiences will involve “leveraging technologies that can be used in various forms and locations” and continuing to move the PlayStation brand beyond its common association of being played on a TV in the living room. More recently in October, there were rumors that Sony might have secured exclusive access to AMD’s next generation graphics tech for a new handheld.

In the meantime, the new PS Portal releases in Japan on December 10 and is up for preorder from November 13 at the same price as the current PS Portal (39,980yen). However, those interested in getting their hands on this model should note that it’s Japanese language only and requires a Japanese PSN account. It will be interesting to see if this new model makes it to other countries and regions.

articles.title: Detective who stole more than £85,000 from own police force jailed
articles.summary: Michelle Kirsty Reason admitted taking money from Derbyshire Police that had been seized from criminals.
articles.body:
A former police detective who stole more than £85,000 from her own force while working in a team that investigated high-level drugs gangs has been jailed.

Acting as the exhibits officer and one of only a small number of people with access to a safe that contained hundreds of thousands of pounds, Michelle Kirsty Reason began siphoning off cash in January 2022, Derbyshire Police said.

According to the force, the 54-year-old spent the money - which had been seized from criminals - on a car, a holiday, and tickets to events.

On Monday, Reason pleaded guilty to theft and misconduct in public office and was jailed for four years and two months at Mansfield Magistrates' and County Court.

Detectives said Reason, of Church Lane in Buxton, was a police exhibits officer based in Ripley.

From about January 2022, the force said Reason began siphoning cash after she dealt with a large cash seizure in the region of £350,000.

She initially stole £15,000 and told officers that, once she found that nobody had noticed, began taking money on a regular basis until she left the force in December 2025.

However, officers then began to review the stored exhibits ahead of an upcoming court case, and began to question where the cash had gone.

Knowing she had been caught out, Reason went to St Mary's Wharf police station to confess to taking the cash.

She gave a full account of the money that had been taken, even bringing with her the empty evidence bags that cash had been seized in, police said.

At the crown court hearing in Mansfield, Reason admitted taking £87,174.05, along with €1,620 and £114 worth of Albanian lek.

Temporary Deputy Chief Constable, Michelle Shooter, said: "Michelle Reason was placed in a position of trust as a detective constable.

"She broke the trust that we as a force put in her, and broke the trust that the public puts in officers to conduct themselves in a right and proper way.

"Her actions are a disgrace. Individuals who are willing to act in such a way have no place in policing and we will do all we can to root them out and bring them to justice."

A further hearing to discuss the case, under the Proceeds of Crime Act, has been listed for 9 April.

articles.title: James Gunn and Peter Safran Are Stepping Down From DC Studios in Shock Exit That Sparks All Sorts of Questions About the DCU
articles.summary: DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down from their roles as co-CEOs, with Skydance tapping an ex-Marvel exec to take over their duties.
articles.body:
DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down from their roles as co-CEOs, with Skydance tapping an ex-Marvel exec to take over their duties.

Skydance confirmed the news in a press release, revealing that Gunn and Safran's last day as studio heads will be on December 1. Former Marvel exec Jeremy Latcham will replace them. Gunn and Safran are still overseeing post-production on Man of Tomorrow, which is directed by the former. They will also remain producers on other DC projects that are already in full swing, such as The Batman Part 2.

“James and Peter launched a new era for DC Studios and led it through a period of real transformation, resetting the foundation and building a slate we’re incredibly proud of," said David Ellison, Chairman and CEO, and Ynon Kreiz, Co-CEO, of Skydance in a joint statement.

DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

"We’re grateful for their passion, contributions and commitment to this legendary brand. Jeremy has been a longtime creative partner to both, and we have complete confidence that James and Peter will ensure a smooth, collaborative transition and continue this work with care. We look forward to working with Jeremy to build the next generation of DC storytelling and to doubling down on our commitment to fans.”

Gunn and Safran also issued their own joint statement, acknowledging they have a history with Latcham from Gunn's days at Marvel.

“Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision," said the duo. "In that time, we helped restore Superman to the heart of DC, while opening new doors and telling new stories in film and television with Peacemaker, Creature Commandos, Lanterns and Clayface. We’re immensely proud of the team that turned that ambition into something real, including the actors, crews and executives we had the opportunity to collaborate with.

9 DC Graphic Novels You Should Read to Understand James Gunn's DCU

"We’ve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and we’re eager to see the perspective he brings to DC’s next chapter. We’re excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lex’s journey in Man of Tomorrow.”

Gunn also released a more personal statement on his socials , where he noted that he has a great time building this universe, but also called the experience "trying" due to the corporate nature of it all. He also stated he is writing at least one more DC movie, but he isn't sure what is in store for him in this universe following the completion of that script.

Gunn and Safran's exit comes as a big surprise, and will likely raise eyebrows across the entertainment industry. Although the press release states they are "stepping away," it's hard not to read between the lines. Just last month, it was reported that the two were safe following the merger approval between Paramount and WB. The merger has led to a lot of key Warner Bros. talent being let go, including executives Pam Abdy and Michael De Luca, who were responsible for curating the studio's lineup of film releases. The news of Gunn and Safran's exit will likely only fuel speculation that they were pushed out by new leadership.

Gunn and Safran had a roughly 10-year plan for the DCU, and we're not even halfway through it and the two are already out the door. For all intents and purposes, the two have only recently suggested that they were continuing to plan out the future of DC. Gunn recently released a podcast talking about what's canon and what's not in the DC Universe , he stated that they are planning to cast their new Batman soon , and emphasized importance on Batman, Superman, and Wonder Woman anchroing this universe . These are not the kinds of words and conversations you'd expect from someone who knows they are going to leave.

The Batman: Part II - Who's Who in Matt Reeves' DC Sequel

Additionally, it's hard not to recontextualize the rumors that Robert Pattinson is in the mix for James Bond following this news. Although The Batman films are not in the DCU, they are overseen by DC Studios. Given the development troubles and set backs for The Batman Part 2 , it's possible that higher-ups at Skydance aren't willing to go through all of this again on a potential third film and they likely want to have one, unified universe to avoid audience confusion.

Regardless of the truth behind Gunn and Safran's departure, their DC tenure was full of ups and downs. Superman was a hit, though has its fair share of detractors who think it's too silly and overstuffed with extra characters. The universe's second film, Supergirl, was a catastrophic bomb . Clayface appears to be a win thanks to its modest budget , despite a somewhat tepid response from critics. Lanterns and Peacemaker were also solid expansions on the TV side of the DCU.

However, the universe has had a difficult time creating momentum. After four years, we really have no idea what's going on with Batman. Wonder Woman is a big question mark. There's been questions over whether or not we'll get a Justice League movie. And other projects that were announced at the outset of this universe, such as Swamp Thing , have seemingly completely stalled out. It hasn't been a disaster, but it definitely seems like things could've been better. Whether the new DC Studios leadership can get a better handle on things remains to be seen.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Dataminers Uncover Potential Majora's Mask, Master Quest DLC Hints
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time players are getting their hopes up after dataminers uncovered hints of Master Quest DLC – and maybe even some Majora's Mask content – tucked in the files of Nintendo's new remake.
articles.body:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time players are getting their hopes up after dataminers uncovered hints of Master Quest DLC – and maybe even some Majora's Mask content – tucked in the files of Nintendo's new remake.

It's not been one week since Nintendo reimagined one of the most critically acclaimed games of all time for Nintendo Switch 2, and while some players are tearing it apart to look for glitches , others are digging even deeper. One of the first things dataminers did was sift through Ocarina of Time's files, and surprisingly, there may be some clues as to what remake plans Nintendo has in the cards.

There's a good chance you're here to see why we're talking about Majora's Mask today. We'll start by saying that you will want to keep expectations in check until an official announcement is made, but that shouldn't make YouTuber Austin John Plays ' findings any less compelling (via Kotaku ).

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Amiibo - Screenshots

Yesterday, the content creator uploaded a video meant to explore the in-game functionality of amiibo for the remake, including unreleased figures, of which there are (officially) two : one for Link, and one for Zelda. Considering the toys-to-life collectibles won't launch until 2027, anyone looking to access the masks they unlock would need to dive into the game's files to use them. This is the path Austin John Plays took – but he found more than just two new masks.

"I was starting to think that this was an Adult Link amiibo that's going to be released in the future," he said, referencing data containing strange, unused NPC dialogue. "I'm starting to not think that. I have a feeling this is one of those videos that I put it out, and in three years, I'm going to go like, 'Look! See? Crazy Austin? Crazy Austin was right!"

The code he referenced in the video alludes to characters calling out Link for wearing a "rare" and "otherworldly." Others call it "strange," with NPC Dampé even saying, "What's with that mask? Lookin' at it makes me feel weird." We do not know what this secret mask looks like or if the text tied to it will ever amount to anything…but with so much data on the backend, you can see why many believe Nintendo has already completed some amount of Majora's Mask content for some reason.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Launch Photos

Again, this is all far from hard evidence, and even if it did point to something related to Majora's Mask, it's hard to say exactly what it may be. Austin John Plays theorizes the data we see here could be tied to a yet-to-be-announced Skull Kid amiibo for a yet-to-be-announced Majora's Mask remake. The idea here is that, like their Nintendo 64 counterparts, Nintendo's work on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake may have allowed it to quickly develop another remake based on Majora's Mask.

There's also the chance that Nintendo could simply release a standalone Skull Kid amiibo. The data could also point to another unique mask entirely – or it could point to nothing at all. Meanwhile, Bluesky user and dataminer @mrcheeze.github.io found their own clues that point to something entirely different: the return of Master Quest.

Master Quest is a remixed, harder mode for the original N64 Ocarina of Time that launched with the GameCube re-release. It reappeared with the Nintendo 3DS remake and then was confusingly absent from the Switch 2 remake. MyCheeze's findings suggest Nintendo could have plans to add it during an update, but dataminer @OatmealDome reported that their findings suggest players will need to own additional DLC in order to access it.

While Nintendo could distribute the DLC for free, I don't see why they went to the effort to make it be unlocked by DLC instead of just including it in an update... (w/ thanks to MrCheeze for initial finding) 🦋 — OatmealDome (@OatmealDome) November 7, 2026

While Nintendo could distribute the DLC for free, I don't see why they went to the effort to make it be unlocked by DLC instead of just including it in an update... (w/ thanks to MrCheeze for initial finding) 🦋

Now, don't get all upset yet; we don't know if this alleged Master Quest DLC will have any particular cost tied to it. It could be $5 or even $20, or it could be some sort of bundle expansion. Nintendo has been known to offer add-on content via certain Nintendo Online subscription tiers, with one of the better examples being Switch 2 upgrades for both The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom .

Oatmeal Dome also added that, based on their findings, the incomplete data also contained references to Master Quest featuring a mirrored world and modified dungeons. Again, it's been only about four days since The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake came to Switch 2. We will only know more with time, so don't go expecting Nintendo to announce Master Quest DLC or a Majora's Mask remake any time soon.

While we wait, you can read our review of the game here , or check out our look at the Biggest Changes from the original 1998 game. Be sure to check out our expanding Ocarina of Time remake Walkthrough for comprehensive guides on each main quest area and dungeon, plus where to get Early Heart Pieces, Early Gold Skulltulas , and Early Item Bag Expansions . If you're looking for more, don't miss our complete guides to All Pieces of Heart , All Gold Skulltulas , and All Empty Bottles .

articles.title: World of Warcraft Forever Dungeon Experience Buffed, but There's a Long Way to Go
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever has been a massive hit, and I've seen hundreds of players in pretty much every part of the game. After Blizzard massively nerfed dungeon experience early on in the Forever beta, the company has finally given it a bit of a buff, but it might not be enough.
articles.body:
World of Warcraft Forever has been a massive hit, and I've seen hundreds of players in pretty much every part of the game. After Blizzard massively nerfed dungeon experience early on in the Forever beta, the company has finally given it a bit of a buff, but it might not be enough.

World of Warcraft Forever community manager Kaivax posted on the WoW forums that dungeon experience would be getting a 50% buff Sunday morning, which did help make dungeons a better way to level your character. But, as the community pointed out, even with this massive 50% buff, the dungeon experience you get is still way less than you'd get in the original version of World of Warcraft classic.

Back when World of Warcraft Forever was first announced, Blizzard's Kris Zierhut did an interview with The Sun talking about how experience from killing monsters in dungeons was "brought way down" The reason he gave for that change was wanting players to focus on leveling out in the open world, saying, "You’d be better off going to Shen’dralas or Riverglades or Hyjal instead of grinding a dungeon. We want people in the outdoor world meeting each other."

On October 8, Blizzard let up a bit, increasing dungeon experience by about 20%. But, because dungeon experience was already around 80% lower than it was on Classic, this 20% buff didn't actually make leveling in dungeons much more viable. Still, Blizzard left it at that level throughout the rest of the beta. Then, over the weekend, as WoW Forever players finally started doing dungeons, it was clear that they just weren't providing enough experience. Enter Sunday's 50% dungeon experience buff.

I actually ran dungeons both on Saturday and Sunday – Ragefire Chasm on Saturday and Ruins of Lordaeron on Sunday – and I did notice a difference. But even though I could tell that my experience bar was filling a bit slower, with the amount of time the dungeons take, you should be able to get one or two full levels out of them. And I'm not alone there; on Reddit, one player even did the math to figure out how far away dungeon experience is from Classic, even with the new buff.

According to aritalo on Reddit , even with the buffs, dungeon enemies are still only rewarding about a third of the experience they do in Classic.

Dungeon experience, even now, is extremely divisive in the community. User InterestingCell5247 writes, "The main problems with dungeons having nerfed exp rates is that its harder to find groups since if you already did the quests you have no reason to go back. But there are also knock-on effects like fewer people feeling incentivized to roll tanks and healers, because those roles generally sacrifice open world leveling speed/efficiency for easier access to dungeons."

Meanwhile, user ACoolGuy-Promise just wishes Blizzard was more clear on the final numbers, saying, "They can’t say “X percent“ of classic values? Just obfuscating this sh*t for no reason. This is barely a buff."

On the forums, however, there are players who are upset that Blizzard caved to the demand for more dungeon experience. For instance, player Kassa posted , "I knew blizzard would cave," and then followed that up by posting, "and I knew even this buff wouldn’t be good enough for the complainers. Blizzard, you have solved nothing. Now they just know to beg louder."

Only time will tell whether or not Blizzard will further buff dungeon experience in WoW Forever, but in the meantime, there does seem to be a ton of players out in the open world. But as more of them filter into World of Warcraft Forever, it's decisions like this that'll decide the shape of the MMO in the years to come. Blizzard has been pretty adament about not changing things that'd alter the spirit of the game, like group tagging . But with this experience change, along with the 20% buff in October, Blizzard is clearly open to tweaking the rate at which players gain experience.

articles.title: World of Warcraft Forever Is the Biggest WoW Launch in History
articles.summary: Even during the beta, World of Warcraft Forever was shaping up to be huge, with an unprecedented amount of testers. But, over the weekend Blizzard announced that World of Warcraft Forever had the biggest launch in WoW history.
articles.body:
Even during the beta, World of Warcraft Forever was shaping up to be huge, with an unprecedented amount of testers. Over the weekend, Blizzard announced that World of Warcraft Forever had the biggest launch in WoW history.

The news came over X/Twitter, where the official World of Warcraft account posted that Forever was the biggest launch in WoW history, both in terms of peak concurrent players and the number of returning players. Keep in mind that this history includes Wrath of the Lich King and Warlords of Draenor, both of which had huge launches – though the latter didn't exactly maintain it.

WoW Forever didn't just break records by dragging old players in and convincing them to resub. Holly Longdale, Blizzard's executive producer and vice president for World of Warcraft, posted her own statistic , saying, "Another statistic is filling our hearts – we are seeing the most NEW players for a WoW launch in 15 years!" That means WoW Forever has brought more players in than any WoW expansion since Cataclysm first launched 16 years ago in 2010.

Congratulations everyone, you made HISTORY! WoW: Forever has achieved: 🔹The biggest launch in WoW history by peak concurrent players 🔹The highest number of returning players in WoW history This is all because of you, the players. From all of us, THANK YOU! — World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) November 7, 2026

Congratulations everyone, you made HISTORY! WoW: Forever has achieved: 🔹The biggest launch in WoW history by peak concurrent players 🔹The highest number of returning players in WoW history This is all because of you, the players. From all of us, THANK YOU!

Scrolling through Longdale's replies, it's clear that people are loving WoW Forever. There are a ton of fans talking about how they played all weekend, like Dungeons and Dragons senior game designer Joey Haeck , who posted a picture of himself on a Zeppelin leaving Orgrimmar, saying, "Congratulations to the whole Forever team! I'm having a blast on every packed zeppelin and every open vista."

While we here at IGN don't have a full review yet, our early review is positive, with reviewer Len Hafer talking about her beta experience , saying, "I ended my beta journey at level 13, gazing out across the dusty plains of Westfall, because I didn't want to spoil too much for myself before the big day. But from what I have seen so far? I think they might have done it. They made me believe I can go home again – and that home is somewhere I want to spend more time, with new surprises to discover. Let's see if they can keep it up for 47 more levels. Watch this space for updates in the weeks to come."

While it's obviously been a huge success, Blizzard had been cooking World of Warcraft Forever on the back burner for a while, only pulling the trigger on its full development after it saw how successful Season of Discovery was back in 2023 . Even with the massive load of players logging in at launch, WoW Forever had an extremely smooth launch , thanks to running on a massive amount of hardware . There was even a race to max level, which took three whole days before someone hit the level cap of 60 .

articles.title: James Gunn and Peter Safran May Be Out, But the DCU Needs to Continue
articles.summary: James Gunn and Peter Safran may be out as co-CEOs of DC Studios, but the last thing Skydance should do right now is reboot the DCU yet again.
articles.body:
In what has proven to be a truly shocking start to the week’s news cycle, James Gunn and Peter Safran are out as the co-CEOs of DC Studios . Stepping up in their place is MCU veteran Jeremy Latcham. It’s the latest shocking turn of events for a division that has certainly seen more than its fair share of turmoil in recent years.

While DC fans are still processing this news, one thing is abundantly clear right now. The last thing the newly unified Skydance needs is for this shake-up to derail the direction of the DC brand. The DCU must continue, with or without Gunn at the helm.

DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

So much of Warner Bros.’s efforts with the DC brand over the past 15 years or so have involved trying to build a proper competitor to Disney and the Marvel Cinematic Universe. They’ve certainly found success with the various solo Batman movies, but building a larger, overarching shared universe has proven much more challenging. 2016’s Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice wasn’t the critical or commercial smash DC needed, and financially, it was mostly downhill from there as far as the DC Extended Universe was concerned.

Nor have the many corporate shake-ups at Warner Bros. helped matters. There have been far too many cooks in the kitchen at DC, which prevented the latter-era DCEU from gaining any sort of storytelling momentum or direction. It’s telling that then-Warner Bros. CEO David Zaslav saw more potential in the Batgirl movie as a tax writeoff than a product worth releasing to the public. DC couldn’t even seem to decide if Ben Affleck, Michael Keaton, or Robert Pattinson should be the main movie Batman going forward. There was no clear plan for the DC line until Gunn and Safran came along in 2023.

It was then that the two co-CEOs unveiled their bold plan for the DCU , dubbed “Chapter 1: Gods and Monsters.” They envisioned an interconnected slate of films and TV shows spread out over the course of many years, all designed to restore the shine of the DC brand and establish a new and cohesive shared universe. The new DCU coalesced in 2025 with the debut of David Corenswet’s Superman , and it expanded this year with the release of Supergirl , Lanterns , and Clayface .

That’s not to say it’s all been smooth sailing for the DCU so far. Superman was a solid success, but Supergirl has proven to be one of the biggest box-office bombs of 2026 , and Clayface has succeeded only by virtue of being a relatively low-budget superhero offering. It’s easy to assume that Supergirl’s performance in particular had some bearing on Skydance’s decision to cut Gunn and Safran loose.

There’s also the fact that the former co-CEOs have faced criticism for not focusing on the biggest names in the DC Comics library. They may have prioritized Superman out of the gate, but what about the DCU versions of Wonder Woman and Batman? Why is Peacemaker getting such a big push before them? Why focus on Clayface before getting Batman himself in order? We suspect that those same questions have been asked in the Skydance boardroom, with the new regime wanting more of a “meat and potatoes” approach to the DC line, rather than Gunn’s more esoteric leanings.

Honestly, that’s not the worst idea. As much as I’ve been looking forward to upcoming DCU projects like Mister Miracle and The People v. Gorilla Grodd , it’s hard to argue against the notion that DC should be focusing more on its core franchises and characters in this early stage of the current cinematic universe. Couple that with the fact that Gunn himself seems almost relieved to be stepping down in his statement, and this shake-up doesn’t have to spell doom for the DC brand.

But that all assumes that Skydance doesn’t completely wipe the slate clean and reboot the DCU entirely. After so many years of corporate chaos and competing creative visions and continuity reboots, the last thing the DC brand needs is for things to start over yet again. We’ve just barely made the transition from the DCEU to the DCU. Don’t make us suffer through all of that again.

It would make Skydance seem incredibly weak if they completely jettisoned the DCU and started things afresh. They need to show moviegoers that they have enough faith in the direction of the DC line to soldier forward, even if the person calling the shots has changed. They need to retain the core continuity that’s been established and key actors like Corenswet, Aaron Pierre’s Green Lantern, and Milly Alcock’s Supergirl. The last thing anyone wants is another long, painful hunt to find the next Superman.

And certainly, the very last thing Skydance needs to do is start nuking the projects Gunn and Safran already have in development. 2027’s Man of Tomorrow is currently in post-production. The People v Gorilla Grodd is well into filming, if not also wrapped at this point. We’d hate to see those projects shelved and given the Batgirl treatment just so we can be subjected to another Superman reboot. That would be a very costly and wasteful mistake on the studio’s part.

The DC line needs a clear and consistent vision, above all else. Whatever your thoughts on the execution of the DCU so far, the fundamentals of Gunn and Safran’s plan have been very sound. The DCU debuted as a shared universe with a rich several-hundred-year history of metahuman activity. It’s meant to be a place where continuity and interconnectivity are less important than allowing writers and directors the chance to leave their mark and let their voices shine. Gunn has often described the DCU approach as being more akin to Star Wars than Marvel, and that’s critical in ensuring that the DCU doesn’t become just another also-ran cinematic universe.

Even if Gunn is no longer at the top of the hill choosing what projects get greenlit, that basic approach needs to continue on. There’s a path forward for Skydance that involves retaining the continuity and general tone of the DCU, but pivoting to focus on the most bankable and recognizable properties.

And that path still has room for Gunn, assuming he and the studio are both still willing to work together post-Man of Tomorrow. Ideally, Gunn will still write and direct new DC projects, whether that’s continuing his Superman saga, tackling more seasons of Peacemaker and Creature Commandos (we know Season 2 is already in the works), or pivoting to other properties that strike his fancy. Gunn already said in his social post about the change in DC management that he has a “secret” script he’s writing for the studio, and heck, he Gunn may be the best option when it comes to finding someone to finally reboot the Dark Knight for the DCU. Gunn can focus more on the actual craft of filmmaking and let others slog through the corporate pressures and responsibilities. A win/win for everyone.

Back in 2023, it felt like Gunn and Safran were exactly the cure DC needed for all of its cinematic woes. That hasn’t entirely panned out in the four years since, but that hardly means those years have been a failure. Skydance can’t throw the Bat-baby out with the bathwater. They need to double down on what’s worked so far in the DCU and build on that, and they – and we – definitely don’t need another reboot.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Zack Snyder Fans Beg DC Studios to 'Restore the Snyderverse' After James Gunn, Peter Safran Exit
articles.summary: Fans of Zack Snyder's DCU are rallying in support of the director following James Gunn and Peter Safran's sudden exit from the franchise.
articles.body:
Fans of Zack Snyder’s DCU are rallying in support of the director following James Gunn and Peter Safran's sudden exit from the franchise.

Gunn revealed he and Safran are leaving DC Studios behind in a lengthy Threads post on November 9, 2026. This news came as quite the surprise, given that Gunn’s version of the DCU is still in its relative infancy; we were just introduced to his Superman in David Corenswet last year, after all.

This unexpected move has once again reignited the conversation surrounding Zack Snyder’s departure from DC Studios a decade ago, which — although it occurred for completely different reasons — has drawn comparisons to Gunn’s current situation and how his movies have performed compared to those of Snyder’s.

"Four years of Zack Snyder's DCEU vs four years of James Gunn's DCU," one said , alongside a screenshot of box office comparisons between the two directors. "You can't fight against the numbers. Snyder's movies outperformed the s**t out of anything Gunn made."

"I swear: If you look at all the Snyderverse demand in the comments and DON'T restore, leadership at Skydance should be hot-swapped out immediately. The fans are literally begging for one thing and one thing only: #RestoreTheSnyderVerse," another demanded .

Fan wars aside, many viewers are hopeful that this means a possible return for Snyder. "Just need ONE vague Zack Snyder Instagram post to put me into hype mode," one user joked.

However, others aren't as optimistic: "Read carefully what [Gunn] said: He is back to pure filmmaking, already has a new project with DC Studios, and the characters they set will live on. As you guys can see, the new guy is from Marvel, not Zack Snyder. The Snyderverse is beyond dead now, more dead than before. That’s the conclusion we are getting, so I don’t know what you guys are celebrating for," another pointed out.

In his statement, Gunn described a dislike for the more "corporate" side of being the head of DC Studios and claimed that he was overworked at the expense of his personal relationships. He and Safran will continue to lead projects that are currently in the works, but beyond that, the characters they have created will go on to have a life of their own.

"That's not to say Peter and I are immediately done with DC or superheroes. We have Man of Tomorrow out this summer. And we've just been engaged on another DC project which I'm writing, and we'll see where it goes after that. And, of course, the characters we set up will live on," Gunn wrote.

This shift puts the future of Gunn's DCU in limbo; thankfully, Lanterns' success has hopes high for a second season , and we still have The People v Gorilla Grodd to look forward to. But beyond this, there’s no telling how this shift in leadership could impact the broader plan for DC movies .
